To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ras gene inhibits the ability of nVDRs to associate with response element sequences in the presence of 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D.

the H-ras oncogene suppresses 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D(3)-regulated vitamin D receptor transcriptional activity in C3H10T(1/2) fibroblast cells, and this suppression is mediated by phosphatidylinositide 3-kinases.
the H-ras oncogene reduces the ability of the vitamin D receptor to associate with response element sequences in the genome.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of nuclear vitamin D resistance induced by the H-rasd gene.
the mechanisms by which ras oncogenes interfere with the transcriptional activity of nVDR.
the mechanisms by which oncogenes interfere with vitamin D receptor-mediated transcriptional activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ras gene suppresses the nVDR transcription by interfering with the ability of the nV DR-RXR complex to bind to response elements.

the H-ras oncogene interferes with the 1, 25(OH)( 2) D-induced transcriptional activity of nVDR in a manner that is independent of the 24-hydroxylation pathway and ERK1/2 and dependent on the PI3K pathway.
the H-ras oncogene inhibits 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D(3)-induced transcriptional activity by interfering with nuclear vitamin D receptor binding to response elements.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the H-ras oncogene suppresses nVDR transcription activity by inhibiting the binding of the nV DR to the VDREs, and this inhibition may be mediated, in part, by PI3K.
the PI3K/Akt pathway is a major mechanism by which the H-Ras gene suppresses 1,25D3-mediated nVDR transcription in C3H10T 1/2 cells.
the PI3K inhibitor, LY294002, restores 1,25 (OH)(2)D3 mediated transcriptional activity in ras cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the H-ras oncogene suppresses nVDR activity by inhibiting the ability of the nV DR to associate with VDREs.
